content.text:
The redesign is in place. The unit tests pass (114 of 114), but the browser tests on the four iPhone/iPad layouts and the offline check are still running; I'll report their result when they finish. Nothing is committed or deployed yet.

**Reference used.** The museum page and the Hungarian site both refused the simple fetch (403). Your mercedes-benz.hu link did load in the local headless browser, so I matched its measured styles:
- **Header and hero:** a black header bar, and a full-width photo hero with a large serif headline.
- **Page and headings:** a white page with dark grey `#333` headings.
- **Cards:** black cards with 12 px corners, where the photo fades into black under a white title.
- **Buttons:** pill-shaped, in MB blue `#0078d6` for the main action, plus a black-pill selector like their brand switcher.

**Index page**
- A black header bar ("Under the skin" on the left, "Unofficial tour notes" on the right), then a full-width hero using the W 196 R hall photo, with a "See the route" button.
- On phones the hero photo sits above the text and fades into black, as on their mobile site.
- Every stop is now a photo card with a "Stop n · year" tag, the car name, its summary and a blue pill listing its mechanisms. Cards are grouped under large room headings ("Legend 1", "Level 8 · 7 stops").
- The cards reuse each stop's existing `photo.jpg`, which the offline cache already stores, so nothing new is downloaded. Images load lazily.

**Stop pages**
- The same black header bar ("← Tour route" and stop position), serif titles and pill-shaped Component/View selectors.
- The 3D view and side panels have rounded corners. The museum-photo overlay still lines up.

**Things you should know**
- **Font:** MB's headline font is proprietary, so I used Instrument Serif instead, a similar condensed serif that is free to use (OFL licence). It is stored locally in `lib/app/fonts/` (21 KB, with its licence file), so offline mode still works.
- **Dark mode is kept:** phones set to dark get a black version of the same design. The header bar, hero and cards stay black in both modes.
- **Photo credit fixed:** the index footer used to credit every photo to Valder137, but the Daimler engine photo is by another photographer. The credit line is now built from each car's photo data.
- **Other edits:** the stop's header bar is now static markup in `stop.html` (the old breadcrumb row was removed from `lib/app/shell.js`), the app colours in `manifest.webmanifest` changed, and CLAUDE.md notes the new design and font.
- **Still to check:** I checked the pages in screenshots at iPhone and desktop sizes, in light and dark, with no console errors and no sideways scrolling. A look on a real iPhone/iPad is still worth doing.

lines: export { tour };
export const loadCars = () => Promise.all(tour.map(async s => (await import(`../../stops/${s.slug}/car.js`)).default));
+// The car.js fields a translation overlay (stops/<slug>/<lang>.js) must cover: page text and the labels subsystems show.
+// Paths use "*" for any array index; legend entries are [token, text] pairs, so only their text is translated.
+const TEXT = [
+  "title", "name", "summary", "eyebrow", "lede", "note", "unverified.*", "photo.alt",
+  "components.*.label", "components.*.talk.*",
+  ...["label", "engineLabel", "legendTitle", "links.*.name", "shapes.*.label", "types.*.label", "presets.*.label",
+    "cases.*.label", "modes.*", "drive.gears.*.name", "legend.*.1"].map(p => `components.*.params.${p}`),
+const RULES = TEXT.map(p => new RegExp(`^${p.replace(/\./g, "\\.").replace(/\*/g, "[^.]+")}$`));
+export const isText = path => RULES.some(r => r.test(path));
+// Every string leaf of v as [path, value], path joined with ".".
+export function leaves(v, path = []) {
+  if (typeof v === "string") return [[path.join("."), v]];
+  if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.flatMap((x, i) => leaves(x, [...path, i]));
+  if (v && typeof v === "object") return Object.entries(v).flatMap(([k, x]) => leaves(x, [...path, k]));
+  return [];
+// The overlay shape for a car with only its text leaves; other array items become null (merge keeps the original).
+export function skeleton(v, path = []) {
+  if (typeof v === "string") return isText(path.join(".")) ? v : undefined;
+  if (Array.isArray(v)) {
+    const items = v.map((x, i) => skeleton(x, [...path, i]));
+    return items.some(x => x !== undefined) ? items.map(x => x ?? null) : undefined;
+  if (v && typeof v === "object") {
+    const out = {};
+    for (const [k, x] of Object.entries(v)) { const s = skeleton(x, [...path, k]); if (s !== undefined) out[k] = s; }
+    return Object.keys(out).length ? out : undefined;
+  return undefined;

content.text:
The site now has an EN/HU switch, and everything a visitor sees is translated to Hungarian: the page text, every panel, button and status message, and all 26 stops. The unit tests (145) and the full Playwright run (140) pass. Nothing is committed or deployed yet.

**How it behaves**
- The **EN | HU** pill sits in the black header bar on the index and on every stop. The page shows its first-ever visit in the browser's language: a Hungarian iPhone gets Hungarian. Once someone switches, that choice is remembered, and it also works offline.
- The switch reloads the page. If the visitor taps it while a stop's 3D view is still loading, that load is simply abandoned.
- The 3D panels switch too, and numbers use a decimal comma (`0,00`, `12,5 liter`, `5,6 LE`). Units follow Hungarian usage: LE instead of PS/hp, `1/min` instead of rpm.
- What stays in English: source titles, URLs and photo credits, and official model names like "300 SEL 6.3".

**Two things I had to fix along the way**
- The headline font file only had basic Latin letters, so ő and ű (as in "műszaki") showed in a different serif. I added the font's extended Latin file (same licence, 7.8 KB). Only pages that use those letters download it.
- Five of the 3D mechanisms broke when the translation function was added, because they already had a variable with the same name. I renamed it, and the existing English tests now cover that.

**What the tests check now**
- **Unit tests:** every on-screen text has a Hungarian translation, there are no leftover unused ones, and placeholders match. Each stop's Hungarian file covers exactly the fields that need translating, with no stray decimal points.
- **Browser test (iPhone):** in Hungarian, all 26 stops show no untranslated text, no errors and decimal commas. The switch works both ways and remembers the choice.

**Worth a look before you deploy**
- I wrote the Hungarian myself, so a native speaker should skim it. Most of it is the per-stop texts (`stops/<slug>/hu.js`); the technical terms are the likeliest to read oddly. Examples: *kis fogaskerék és fogaskoszorú* for the Reitwagen's pinion and ring gear, and *Eleje le: szoros rakodás* for "Front end down: nest the cars".
- I wrote it in the formal address ("Figyelje", "Válasszon").
- I added one detail that isn't in the English: the 220 S text calls Béla Barényi *magyar származású* (of Hungarian descent).

I also updated CLAUDE.md: how new text gets translated, and that each new stop needs a `stops/<slug>/hu.js`. There's an untracked `research_pt2.md` in the repo that I didn't create or touch.

Want me to commit, push and redeploy?

Add a Hungarian version and a three-car teaser page

language and the choice is remembered. UI text goes through t() with an
English-keyed catalog (lib/app/i18n/hu.js); each stop has stops/<slug>/hu.js
over car.js's text fields. Readouts use a decimal comma; the headline font gets
its latin-ext subset for ő and ű.

teaser.html lists the Blitzen-Benz, 300 SL and 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé with
the index's look and offline behaviour; opened from it, those stop pages page
between the three and link back to the teaser.

teaser's paging and offline load.

EOF
